what_happened: Job 20261103-162416-m9th ("Pause an item that fails twice; stop the batch only on shared causes", code) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic found the fix location right (the unconditional set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure) in Drain::finish), the split of landing errors and the reuse of StopCause::of sound, and the demonstration seams real. One major finding remained. The plan classes every Err from RealSteps::run and from a read as a shared host or Athena cause. Many of those Err texts are verdicts on the item's own job ("job X was declined", "is already closed", "has N readings"). After names and digits are masked, two unrelated items hitting the same sentence get the same key and would stop the batch falsely, which is the fault the request is meant to fix. Minor: the shared no-outcome test case uses invented text that no production path produces. Nit: masking of ids wrapped in backticks or parentheses depends on trimming and needs a unit test. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that the seams a plan names exist. It does not require the plan to trace a classification claim ("these Err arms carry host and Athena errors") through the code that produces those errors. The plan asserted the claim from the arms' position and a risk bullet, though grepping the bail! sites in go_with_stages and pin.rs would have settled it. The test scripts invent a shared-cause text instead of using real error texts, so the plan's own demonstrations cannot expose the gap. Planning has three fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan, and has no repair step for a defect the code can answer. A major finding left in round 3 therefore loses all planning spend. The change is also to a core flow, the drain, where many error sources interact.
prevention: Make the planning stage, for any plan that classifies errors or states into categories, enumerate the real producers of each class from the code (every bail!/Err site feeding the arm) and list them in the plan with their classification. Have the critic check that list against the code in round 1. Require demonstrations to use texts taken from those real sites. Also keep the last good plan and allow one targeted repair round for a single remaining major finding, instead of discarding the plan.
proposed_request: Pause an item that fails twice and stop the drain only on causes shared across items. Today Drain::finish sets Stop::RepeatedFailure unconditionally (drain.rs around 2379). Outcome: an item that fails twice for reasons of its own is paused, and the drain goes on to the next item. The drain stops only when the failure evidence shows a shared host or Athena cause, such as disk, login or usage limit (reuse StopCause::of), or the same failure across different items that does not come from a verdict on the item's own job. Before planning the classification, list every Err site that feeds the run and read arms (go_with_stages in run/mod.rs, pin.rs, and the landing_from_report Ok/Err split) and mark each as item-specific or shared. Item-specific texts such as "job X was declined", "is already closed", "is running", "was interrupted" and "has N readings, the most a job may have" must never count as shared, even if they match across items after masking. Only a recognised shared cause, such as a StopCause match or a host or network error, may stop the batch. Acceptance: (1) two different items each failing twice with the item-specific texts above are both paused and the drain finishes the rest of the queue; (2) an item failing twice with a real StopCause (low disk, expired login) stops the batch; (3) a landing error is classified by where it arises; (4) demonstrations use real error texts from those sites, not invented ones; (5) a unit test shows that ids wrapped in backticks or parentheses are masked. Test with drain::drain and the Stub, and add a CHANGELOG entry.
